band_change_evidence_test.required: at least 2 independent sources with at least 1 at sourceTier >= 4
band_change_evidence_test.reason: Federal court rulings in Nazemian et al. v. Databricks (N.D. Cal.) reported by Bloomberg Law and Publishers Lunch (tier 4), plus the company's published AI Governance Framework and Responsible AI documentation (tier 3). Multiple independent sources, at least one at tier 4.

key_evidence: Databricks publishes more governance material than any other lab in Cluster B. Its AI Governance Framework and responsible AI documentation set out an ethics, transparency and interpretability pillar, and it gives them away for the whole field to use.

None of it is measured. There is no outcome data on whether the framework changes anything, no workforce data, no failure disclosure, and no independent audit. Databricks is private and discloses accordingly.

Authors sued Databricks in March 2024 alleging its MosaicML models were trained on Books3, a dataset of nearly 197,000 pirated books. Courts have split the case: the direct claims over DBRX were dismissed, and the claims over MPT continue. Nothing is decided and nothing here is scored as proven harm.
The published 48.4 implied formal pathways and some outcome data across all eight areas. Databricks has framework documents and no outcome data at all.
The score falls 17.1 points, the smallest fall in Cluster B, because Databricks genuinely publishes more than its cluster peers.

evidence.claim: The Databricks AI Governance Framework sets out pillars for governing AI deployments, including an Ethics, Transparency and Interpretability pillar covering fairness, accountability and human oversight.
Databricks describes an Ethics, Transparency and Interpretability pillar that supports organisations in building trustworthy and responsible AI systems.
The judge denied the defendants' motion to dismiss, stating: Defendants may ultimately prevail on this issue, but for now, Plaintiffs' allegations are sufficient.
evidence.source: Publishers Lunch on the authors' copyright suit against Databricks

evidence.claim: Judge Breyer dismissed the direct copyright infringement claims against Databricks over its DBRX model, while the proposed class of authors retains pending infringement claims over MPT, created by Databricks unit MosaicML.
evidence.source: Bloomberg Law on the Databricks copyright rulings

evidence.claim: Authors allege their works were part of a dataset of nearly 197,000 books, the Books3 dataset, used to train Databricks' MosaicML models.
evidence.source: Databricks large language model litigation summary

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A DOWNGRADE. No score change is proposed for application. The published 48.4 is a never-assessed uniform-seed placeholder shared byte-for-byte with seven other ai-labs entities at consecutive alphabetical ranks; the rank is an artefact of the tie. No adverse conduct was located. The entire gap measures disclosure, not conduct. Applying a one-off baseline reset on evidence-absence alone would convert a calibration problem into a conduct finding, which the anti-false-positive screen forbids. Referred for coordinator-level calibration of the ai-labs 60.9 and 48.4 uniform-seed clusters. rotation-state composite/band/rank left at the PUBLISHED values.
